Permanent record ID: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.21739.result

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Eleven US native-English adult participants produce 200 conversations with eight anonymized original models. Diagnostic data are self-reported; conversations are not independent participants.
  • GPT-4o-mini suggests question subsets that participants may revise. Golden responses are participant-edited after viewing original and preference-informed model outputs, rather than independent wholly human-written references.
  • Eleven evaluation models predict participant annotations. Default does not use future turns; Omniscient includes privileged profiles. Mistral Large draft scores and Kendall tau are supplementary and excluded from the Composite.
  • Pooled tests assume conversation independence despite repeated participants. Conversation-level Pearson r=-0.097 and model-level Spearman rho=-0.36 have different statistical units and are not interchangeable.
  • The human baseline has three raters and seven conversations. Small imbalanced culturally restricted samples and self-report limit interpretation; the authors explicitly exclude clinical validation and safety-critical deployment use.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Chartography uses 100 professionally authored chart questions verified by three additional experts and screened for at least one meaningful frontier-model failure. Each configuration receives 20 no-tools trials per task; Gemini 3.5 Flash judges the final answer against expert targets/ranges without seeing the chart, and multipart answers require all parts.

Permanent record ID: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2608.10677.method

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • The benchmark has 100 selected tasks, twelve domain labels and 98 byte-distinct images. Professionals select/create charts, write objective questions, walkthroughs and ranges; three additional experts verify each task and at least one frontier failure is required for retention.
  • Twenty no-tools trials per task yield 2,000 scored responses per configuration, not 2,000 independently sampled tasks. Gemini 3.5 Flash grades equivalence to expert answers/ranges without seeing the chart; multipart answers are all-or-nothing and its own leaderboard entry is self-judging.
  • Table 3 freezes the July 2026 snapshot, reporting mean pass@1 and 95% confidence intervals. Display ranks and overlapping intervals do not establish statistically distinct capability tiers.
  • Eighty-one charts are online-sourced and nineteen are author-created. Provenance is reported; this repair does not independently establish redistribution rights for each image.
  • Failure explanations derive from qualitative trajectory review. This author did not audit judge validity, CI coverage or task corpus, and does not interpret the explanations as a controlled perception-versus-reasoning causal ablation.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The experiment applies one GSPO epoch with a rank 32 LoRA adapter to Kimi K2.7 Code on 1000 expert-built repository tasks and 700 terminal tasks, without a supervised stage. Reward is target-check fraction, but any failed pass-to-pass regression test zeroes repository reward; terminal tasks have no such regression-test gate.

Scope and reported basis

Measurement scope
paper-reported; author did not independently reproduce experiments

Permanent record ID: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2610.00890.method

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Experts author 1,000 repository-change tasks and 700 terminal tasks. RL is used without a supervised stage; regression tests gate repository reward, while terminal tasks have no pass-to-pass gate.
  • Partial credit is over equally weighted checks/verifier criteria, not necessarily one vote per semantic requirement; a requirement can map to one or more checks.
  • Headline DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench 2.1 baselines are public scores. The in-house DeepSWE baseline differs; Terminal-Bench 2.1 has no in-house base run, and its public baseline averages three runs.
  • Terminal-Bench 4 revises Terminal-Bench 3 and forms one family for pooled analysis. Eight trained Terminal-Bench 3 runs were excluded for harness failures, leaving eight passes among 66 scored runs.
  • The report uses one final trained checkpoint/run. Paired behavioral examples focus on newly solved tasks and do not isolate causal effects of each task or reward property.
